children.description: An operating system is a software that manages computer hardware and provides common services to computer programs.
The types of operating systems include single-user, multi-user, and multi-tasking OS.
The primary functions of an operating system include process management, memory management, file management, and I/O management.
Process concepts include process creation, process control, and process termination.
Process synchronization techniques include monitor, semaphores, and locks.
A deadlock is a situation where two or more processes are blocked, waiting for each other to release resources.
CPU scheduling algorithms include First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Job First (SJF), Priority Scheduling, and Round Robin (RR).
CPU scheduling parameters include arrival time, burst time, and priority.
Memory management techniques include contiguous allocation, fragmentation, and virtual memory.
Paging is a memory management technique that divides the address space of a process into fixed-size blocks called pages.
Virtual memory concepts include page tables, page fault handling, and demand paging.
Virtual memory advantages include improved memory utilization, reduced memory requirements, and improved program execution.
Segmentation techniques include fixed-size segmentation and variable-size segmentation.
Segmentation advantages include improved memory utilization, reduced memory requirements, and improved program execution.
Disk scheduling algorithms include First-Come-First-Served (FCFS), Shortest Seek Time First (SSTF), andSCAN.
Disk scheduling parameters include disk head movement, disk seek time, and disk rotation speed.
File system types include hierarchical file systems, network file systems, and flash file systems.
File system organization includes directory hierarchy, file allocation, and file organization.
